newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue-chips record gains, ITC in limelight.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue-chips record gains, ITC in limelight.

text.p: Bombay share prices finished higher on Wednesday as short-covering by operators kept most blue-chip stocks in positive terrritory, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rose 47.88 points or 1.55 percent to a provisional close of 3,128.14. The day's high was 3,135.69.
"There was a lot of short-covering in pivotals that helped the market rally," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
The National Stock Exchange (BSE) 50-stock index was up 4.0 points or 0.45 percent to 895.0.
Traders said speculators who had short-sold last week were squaring off positions.
Shares of front-bencher ITC gained 12.50 rupees or 4.9 percent to 264.0 rupees with more than 1.09 million shares traded at the BSE.
Market participants said short-covering in ITC after the stock attracted backwardation charges at the close of BSE's weekly account last week fuelled the price rise.
Backwardation is a charge on short sellers to carry-forward transactions from one settlement to another. It reflects large oversold positions.
Foreign funds were bidders in pivotal stocks that included BSES, TISCO, Bajaj Auto, Tata Chem and TELCO, dealers said.
The 500-share CRISIL index ended 4.11 points, or 0.69 percent, higher at a provisional 599.68.
SBI rose 5.50 rupees to 222.50, TISCO 1.75 to 168.50, TELCO 16.0 to 416.25, Reliance 1.25 to 185.50, Bajaj Auto 10.50 to 943.75, BSES 7.75 to 199.75 and L&T 2.50 to 223.50.
